caption:
Can an insurer reject a life claim on a policy that's more than 3 years old?

Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act, a life policy can't be questioned on any ground once 3 years have passed.
Within those 3 years, the insurer can question it for fraud or for hiding a fact that matters to the risk.
The 3 years count from the latest of: policy issue or risk start, revival of a lapsed policy, or adding a rider. So a revived policy restarts the clock.
The safest path is still to disclose everything honestly in the proposal form.
